correctness.rationale: The 36 constrained oriented three-mers form exactly 18 reverse-complement pairs. The eight-vertex undirected quotient of the 12-vertex overlap digraph has four odd vertices AT, TA, CG, GC (degree three) and four even vertices (degree six). Euler parity prohibits a perfect one-occurrence path or circuit; the only odd-to-odd target edges are ATA/TAT and CGC/GCG, giving necessary exact repeated classes at lengths 19 open and 20 closed windows. Two explicit words attain the bounds. A terminating exact integer recurrence over 18-bit coverage masks and duplicate flags proves 57,984 linear optima and 289,920 rooted circular optima; primitive-period reasoning divides by 20. A separately written DFS verifier without memoization checks these counts independently across 3,221,436 nodes. Every counted word is in the stated homopolymer-free alphabet and covers all required classes. Infinite-alphabet extrapolation is not claimed.

evidence: Orenstein and Shamir prove that all unconstrained odd-order reverse-complement classes can be covered once and present optimal even-order sequences and tables; their source set includes all 64 oriented DNA three-mers.

The 2026 run-restricted universal-cover theorem forbids a run of one distinguished letter and covers every permitted ORIENTED factor, with no reverse-complement identification; its hypotheses and conclusions do not give this all-homopolymer, orbit-coverage result.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither theorem applies after simultaneously forbidding AA, CC, GG, TT and replacing all targets by reverse-complement orbit representatives. General minimal-postman algorithms can compute finite instances but do not entail the evaluated complete exact equality counts.

originality.rationale: Orenstein–Shamir (2013) treat the unrestricted reverse-complement k-mer completion problem, proving the odd-k lower bound sharp in that unrestricted graph; the all-letter homopolymer constraint changes the graph and introduces a genuine odd-vertex obstruction. Burris–Motta–Shipman (2016) supply an unoriented reversal quotient framework but neither the DNA complementation variant nor the constrained exact equality census. Fully read published related dinucleotide and forbidden-one-run results have different target sets, order, or coverage semantics, and their statements do not imply these specific numeric counts. value.rationale: The specific object is motivated before computation by constrained DNA-probe design: 3-mers without identical neighbors, opposite-strand equivalence, and both circular and linear synthesis formats. The result isolates a parity-based obstruction that distinguishes the constrained setting from an unrestricted odd-order theorem, gives sharp exact overhead of one linear and two circular windows, identifies precisely which motifs must repeat, and counts all optimizer designs. These structural and complete-classification facts have plausible value for benchmark construction and probe design flexibility; they are not arbitrary recomputations of a known table. No downstream biological efficacy is inferred.
